analytic.title: Formal Schedulability Analysis and Simulation for AADL

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: With rapid developments in science and technology, we now see the ubiquitous use of different types of safety-critical systems in our daily lives such as in avionics, consumer electronics, and medical systems. In such systems, unintentional design faults might result in injury or even death to human beings. To make sure that safety-critical systems are really safe, only using the traditional methods is not enough. Model-Driven Architeture (MDA) method is becoming the mainstream as the instrument of the people. Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) is a modeling language standard brought forward by the Society of Automotive Engineers, Avionics Systems Division, et al, is becoming a research topic for many organizations and institutes. It is a kind of MDA method also. For safety-critical systems, we must verify all the important properties whatever the method we use. Among the properties, the schedulability problem is a very important problem in the real-time software. But, how to solve the schedulability problem in a practical AADL project is a new obstacle to us. In this paper, we use the linear hybrid automata to abstract the semantics of the software components explicitly, then try to use TIMES tool developed by Uppsala Univ and Furness tool developed by Fremont Associates, LLC to simulate the semantics of linear hybrid automata and the scheduling execution trace of AADL software components respectively. Finally, we compare the two methods and make a conclusion.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Embedded system is a kind of particular computation systems designed for executing real-time computation and embedded in other physical systems usually. Embedded systems are applied by people in so many safety-critical domains, including avionics, automotive electronics, or robotics systems which all need timing requirements, fault and error behaviors, time and space partitioning, and safety and certification properties. Because of their application domains and strict requirements, how to ensure the high safety and security of the embedded real-time software in embedded systems is a big problem. With the increase of the magnitude and the complexity of the embedded software, the development time and cost keep increasing. So, how to design the software effectively is a problem and need be solved first. Fortunately, people invent many modern software development technologies and methods now, such as formal methods in modern software engineering, Model-Driven Architecture (MDA), Aspect-Oriented methods, Component-Based methods, etc. Among them, MDA is the method which has better life force and more application foreground than other methods. Figure 1 shows the software development process using MDA method. Using model design, the models become the center of the research. From the other side, the model is the abstract denotation of the system. So, modeling is a basic method to restrict the complexity of the system. In the industry of the embedded software, there are already so many function-oriented modeling tools, such as Simulink, SCADE [1], UML.

The most important characters of embedded realtime software distinguishing from universal software are not only the complexity of functional requirements, but also the constraints of non-functional requirements, such as reliability, availability, timing, responsiveness, throughput, safety and security. The non-functional properties of each single module are satisfied much easier than that of a whole system, so how to satisfy the non-functional properties of the whole system brings new obstacles and new challenges to developers.

To solve this, the trend of MDA method is considering the non-functional requirement specification from the perspective of the architecture of the whole system, then disassemble the non-functional properties to the underlayer, illustrated in Figure 2. ( In this figure, the component model is corresponding to the "model" module in Figure 1)We use Airbus Co. as an example [12], in its whole development frame, because of using the "modeldriven development, correct-by-construction" method, the coding errors are much less although the magnitude of software is bigger and bigger. In the software of A310, the average errors per 100KB code are several hundred. In the software of A320, the average errors per 100KB code are less than one hundred. In the software of A340, the average errors per 100KB code are less than ten and the code generated automatically is the 70% of the entire code.

AADL [10] is a textual and graphical language used to design and analyze the software and hardware architecture of performance-critical1 real-time systems. It can be used to describe functional interfaces to components (such as data inputs and outputs) and performance-critical aspects of components (such as timing). The AADL can also be used to describe how components interact, such as how data inputs and outputs are connected or how application software components are allocated to execution platform components. The most importance is that AADL is developed to meet the special needs of performancecritical real-time systems, including embedded realtime systems such as avionics, automotive electronics, or robotics systems. The language can describe important performance-critical aspects such as timing requirements, fault and error behaviors, time and space partitioning, and safety and certification properties. Such a description allows a system designer to perform analysis of the composed components and systems such as system schedulability, sizing analysis, and safety analysis. From this analysis, the designer can evaluate architectural tradeoffs and changes.

There are two major categories of components in AADL: software components and execution platform components. The semantics of each software component is in the form of hybrid automaton. So, the best way for design the analysis and simulation methods of the software components of AADL is consistent with their semantics. Unfortunately, there are few tools for AADL which are consistent with the semantics mentioned above. For example, the Furness toolset is primary tool for simulation the AADL code. But it is realized by stochastic evaluation and statistic charts. The different semantics between the hybrid automaton and statistics is a big gap for simulating the whole activities in AADL.
Specific contributions of this paper are as follows:

Although AADL states its semantics being of the hybrid automata, it just introduces the behaviors of the software components briefly. We define the concept of the linear hybrid automata formally, and use that concept to describe the behaviors of the software components. Unlike the work of Literature [11], we abstract the semantics of software components in advance, so we do the analysis work in the design phase, simulate the behaviors of the software components and correct the errors in the early phase to reduce the cost.
To ensure the safety of the model, the judgement of the schedulability is one of the necessary steps.

In the design phase, we use two leading tools to simulate the scheduling execution trace respectively, and compare the results to make a conclusion. The rest of this paper is organized as follows: Section 2 discusses related work. Section 3 presents the linear hybrid automata model of the thread components. Section 4 presents the simulation process using the two tools respectively. We conclude in section 5 with future research directions.

div.head: Related work
div.p: More and more people realize that the nonfunctional properties in embedded real-time system are hard to meet. Although the test process can reduce the errors markedly, it can not be applied until the system being realized. In this phase, the cost of the correcting errors is much more than the cost of the same activity in the design phase. So, without disputation, the formal method is first choice to people in the design pahse. In academe, there are so many formal methods for the embedded real-time systems, such as timed automata, hybrid automata, interface automata, CSP, LTL, CTL, Lustre, etc. A hybrid automaton [4] is an anstract of a dynamical system with both discrete and continuous components. A linear hybrid automaton [4,9] is one kind of hybrid automata which is under broad application.

MetaH [2] is an architecture description language, developed at Honeywell Technology Laboratories under the sponsorship of the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) and US Army Aviation and Missle Command (AMCOM). Because of its extensive application fields and successful application cases, the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) presents a standard named Architecture Analysis & Design Language (AADL) from MetaH.

Literature [11] presents a method to abstract the semantics of the software components in the executing phase, in other words, it do not abstract the semantics until the system being realized. Its defect is that the cost of correcting the errors is much more than the cost in the design phase.

There are some toolsets which supports the AADL, such as Furness toolset, ADes toolset, etc. But, neither the Furness toolset nor the ADeS toolset has the capacity to analyse the all activities of the software components. We will show the problem of the aforementioned two toolsets is that we hard to say the system is schedulability intuitively from the simulation results. And there are few tools which has hybrid automtata semantics to do the scheduling analysis. Considering this reason, we use the TIMES tool whose semantics is a timed automaton extended with task to simulate the some behaviors of the software components of AADL and judge the schedulability intuitively.

TIMES [3,6,7,8] is a modeling and schedulability analysis tool for embedded real-time systems, developed at Uppsala University in 2001. It is appropriate for systems that can be described as a set of preemptive or non-preemptive tasks which are triggered periodically or sporadically by time or external events. It provides a graphical interface for editing and simulation, and an engine for schedulability analysis. The most important thing is that the semantics of TIMES is a timed automaton extended with taks which has the same root as hybrid automaton. Because of this reason, we will show it has the better effects to simulate the part of the behaviors of the software components than the result of Furness tool.

div.head: The formal models of AADL
div.p: Discrete and temporal semantics of a single software component of AADL is defined using a linear hybrid automata notation. We first give the definition of hybrid automata like below: Definition 1. A hybrid automaton H consists of the following components: Variables. A finite set X={x 1 , x 2 ,…, x n }of realnumbered veriables. The number n is called the dimension of H. We write X for the set { 1

x … n x } of dotted variables which represent first derivatives during continuous change, and we write X ' for the set The vertices in V are called locations. The edges in E are called transitions or edges. Initial, invariant, and flow conditions. Three location labeling functions init, inv, and flow that assign to each location v∈V three predicates. Each initial condition init(v) is a predicate whose free variables are from X. Each invariant condition inv(v) is a predicate whose free variables are from X. Each flow condition flow(v) is a predicate whose free variables are from X∪ X . Jump conditions. An edge labeling function jump that assigns to each edge e∈E a predicates. Each jump condition jump(e) is a predicate whose free variables are from X∪X ' .

div.head: Events.
div.p: A finite set ∑ of events, and an edge labeling function event: E→ ∑ that assigns to each edge an event.

Basing on this definition, let's define the concept of the linear hybrid automata: Definition 2. A linear hybrid automaton L is a tuple: L=(Z, X, V, E, V 1 , α, β, γ), where Z is a finite set of system states; X is a finite set of real-value variables; V is a finite set of locations; E ⊆ V×V×φ×Ψ gives the set of transitions. An edge<v, φ, Ψ, v'>represents a transition from location v to location v' under the conditions of variable constraints φ(a≤x≤b), Ψ is the set of reset actions (y:=c), x, y∈X, a, b, c∈R; V 1 is the set of initial locations; α is label function which maps each location into one of the state in Z; β is a label function which maps each location into a set of { 1

x … n x } (each n x has the form of n x =a, x∈X, a∈R), for each x∈X, there is only one x =a∈β(v); γ is a label function which gives each location a set of initial conditions (each one has the form of x=a, x∈X, a∈R).

In AADL standard, there are five kinds of software components, Data, Subcomponent, Thread, Thread group and Process. Data components represent data types and static data in source text. They are sharable between threads within the same thread group or process, and across processes and systems. The subprogram component models callable source text that is executed sequentially. It is callable from within threads and subprograms. Threads represent sequential sequences of instructions in loaded binary images produced from source text. Threads model schedulable units of control that can execute concurrently. Threads can interact with each other through exchanges of control and data as specified by port connections, through server subprogram calls, and through shared data components. A thread group is a compositional component that permits organization of threads within processes into groups with relevant property associations. A process represents a virtual address space. A complete process specification must contain at least one thread declaration. Among these components above, only thread component models a schedulable unit that transitions between various scheduling states and it equals the task in operating systems. So, the scheduling analysis is involved with thread components.

In this paper, we use linear hybrid automata to model the thread locations and actions, according to the AADL standard. We use the notations of literature [5] for extending the predicates on the transition edges, illustrated as Figure 3. A thread goes through several locations. The initial location is Initial_Location. When the loading of the virtual address space as declared by the enclosing process completes, a thread is initialized by performing an initialization code sequence in the source text. Once initialization is completed the thread enters the Suspend_Await-ing_Dispatch_Location if the thread is part of the initial mode, i.e. the variable In_current_mode is true, otherwise it enters the Suspend_Awaiting_Mode_ Location. When a thread is in the Suspend_Awaiting _Mode_location, it cannot be dispatch for execution. Because this thread is not in the current mode. The change rate of Compute Execution Time c i =0 in all locations except Computation_Location. Computation _Location is a composite location, we will discuss later. The locations of a thread switch between the Suspend_Awaiting_Mode_Location and Suspend_ Awaiting_Dispatch_Location by the transitions labeled by event Activation or Deactivation. The symbol ? denotes that the corresponding event is true or not when it is triggered by the dispatcher. Event Activation/Deactivation is true when the thread is/isn't in the new mode.

So, the transitions from Suspend_Awaiting_Mode_Location, Suspend_Awaitin-g_Dispatch_location and Computation_ Location to Halt_Location are triggered by the event stop. The transition from Computation_Location to Halt_ Location can be triggered by the event error also. Wait_For_Dispatch is an invariant in location Suspend_Awaiting_Dispatch_Location. Enable(t) is a function whose values are distinguished in different kind of threads. For a periodic thread, the Enable(t) is t=Period. The Wait_For_Dispatch invariant is the formula t≤Period. The dispatch occurs at t= Period. For a sporadic thread, the Enable(t) is formula t≥Period. The Wait_For_Dispatch invariant is the formula true. For a aperiodic thread, the Enable(t) is the formula true and the Wait_For_Dispatch invariant is the formula true.

div.head: The top level hybrid automata of one thread component
div.p: Figure 4 shows the refined locations in Computa-tion_Location. Only the change rate of execution time in running location is c =1. And the invariant in running location is c≤the_worst_case_ET. It means that the computing execution time must not exceed the worst case execution time. When c>the_worst_case_ ET, the dispatcher will trigger the event error. The events abort, awaiting, ready, running, complete, resume, preempt, block and unblock are triggered by the dispatch. So, the Figure 3 and Figure 4 show the exact semantics of each thread. Literally, a state of a thread will be a triple (l, u, q) consisting of a location l, a clock valuation u, and a thread queue q. The thread queue is maintained by the scheduler. Each semantic hybrid automaton defines semantics for a single component. A process component may contain several thread components, and a system component may contain multiple process components. So, the semantics of components in the upper level is defined to be the concurrent composition of the semantics of the components in the lower level. The single semantic hybrid automaton is of each thread component. And, how to compose them has already discussed detailedly in [4].

div.head: Simulation
div.p: In the design phase, after the design work, a necessary work we need to do is the simulation. The benefits of simulation are that we correct the errors in the models much easier than in the code, the cost of the correcting in the early development phase is much less than the cost in the late phase. So, simulation is the next step of design. In this paper, we just consider the schedulability property. Although there are some tools of hybrid automata for model checking, they do not aim at schedulability. So, we abstract the semantics of thread components using the linear hybrid automata, and use two tools to verify respectively, and compare the results. One way is to use the Furness toolset to simulate the scheduling executing trace, the other way is to use the TIMES tool to simulate the scheduling executing trace.

div.head: Furness Toolset
div.p: Furness toolset supports modeling, the scheduling analysis and execution simulation. For example, there are three threads T1, T2, T3 in a process of the system. All of them are bounded in a single processor component which is an abstract of scheduling mechanism. The main parameters of a thread component include Period Time, Compute Execution Time, the Best Case Execution Time and the Worst Case Execution Time, Deadline, etc. We evaluate T1(15,3..5,3,5,15) ( The symbol .. denotes the span of the compute execution time), T2(20, 3..5,3,10,20), T3(25,3..5,3, 15,25).

The Figure 5 is the picture which shows the scheduling analysis results. The y-axis of Figure 5 denotes the statistic times of the executing time of each thread ending at the time instants of the x-axis, i.e., it denotes the probability of each thread ending at the time instants of the x-axis. According to the probability values, the Simulator VXP.exe of Furness toolset may simulate the execution trace, illustrated in Figure 6. We have concluded the two shortcomings of the analyzer and the simulator of Furness toolset. First, , not the answer that the set of threads are schedulability or not. Neither gives us a counterexample to illustrate how the deadline breaks. So, we can not get the schedulability answer from the results directly. Secondly, neither the analyzer nor the simulator has the semantics in the form of hybrid automata. So there must be some difference between the modeling and the simulating more or less. And another shortcoming of Furness is that it can not support the simulation involved in the modes. Modes represent the operational states of software, execution platform, and compositional components in the modeled system. Mode transitions model dynamic operational behavior that represents switching between configurations and changes in components internal characteristics. So, modes are very useful elements in AADL and almost all the integrated programs are involved in the mode transitions. But, its simulating process may be very complex. So, the Furness toolset has not provided this function yet.

div.head: Times tool
div.p: Considering the defects of the Furness toolset, we use TIMES tool to model the thread components of AADL and to simulate the scheduling executing trace of them. The reason we choose TIMES tool is that it has the semantics in terms of timed automata, which is the derivation of hybrid automata. That is, we use extended timed automata to simulate the hybrid automata for schedulability. We will show that the models in TIMES tool can solve the verification and simulation problem effectively without the switch of the modes than Furness toolset.

The TIMES tool has realized the dispatcher implicitely. Only things we should do are modeling the threads directly. We give an example below to illustrate how to model the threads and how to use TIMES to simulate the behaviors of the scheduling trace.

There are four threads in one process bounded in a single, task_A, task_B, task_C and task_D. Task_A is an aperiodic thread, illustrated in Figure 7. Its execution time is 1. The arriving time instant of the first iteration of task_A is at clock y=60. When y＞ 60,the location OFFSET will switch to LOC_2. When the x= =3, the transitions from LOC_2 are nondeterministic to LOC_2 or LOC_3. Task_B's parameters are (20, 5, 20) (Period, the Worst Case Execution Time, Deadline). It means that in TIMES we must set the value of the best case execution time equals to the value of the worst case execution time. If not, the result is not decidable [6]. Task_C's parameters are (30, 8, 28). Task_D is a sporadic thread, and its parameters are (30, 5, 30). The Period of a sporadic thread means that the arriving time interval of a sporadic thread must not less than the Period value. And the scheduling algorithm is preemptive EDF. When we finish the modeling process, the next works to do are verification and simulation. First, we need to do the syntax checking. If the answer is yes, we do the schedulability analysis. If the threads are schedulable, it will show yes also. If the threads are not schedulable, it will show the possible executing trace. In Figure 8, the arrows↑means the task arriving time, the arrows ↓means the deadline. For our model, the set of the threads is not schedulable, and we show the trace in the Figure 8. It means that in Figure 7, if the transition from LOC_2 to LOC_2 happens six times continuously, the threads are not schedulable obviously at the seventh iteration. We also could see the dynamic simulation trace of the models.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: A key concern of our work of this paper is to abstract the semantics of software components of AADL using linear hybrid automata in the design phase statically and use two different tools to simulate the scheduling executing trace in the design phase also. From the section 4, we can see the TIMES tool is more effective in simulation than the Furness toolset. That is because the semantics of TIMES is a set of timed automata which is the derivation of linear hybrid automata. So, actually, we use timed automata to simulate the linear hybrid automata. That's the reason why the TIMES tool is more effective than Furness tool. But the shortage of TIMES is that the TIMES tool does not aim at AADL, it does not include the concept of mode. And it can not model the thread components directly, just by handwork now. The future work for us is that we will design a toolset which has the exact semantics of linear hybrid automata to cover the whole process from the modeling to the simulating.
